ground_truth_evidence: category 5: the dataset's own trigger (newplatform_bundles/conversion/c5/gt/espeak-ng/vulnerability_WF_LLM_3/input-001; adapted: the conversion replay's input-001 (exploit payload #2: `<speak><prosody volume="2147483647">test</prosody></speak>`); the exploit tries 5 payloads and stops at the first failure without recording which. Self-check confirms it crashes the vulnerable build (stack-buffer-overflow in ProcessParamStack) and not the secure one; verified locally against espeak-ng @80f7d5d with the WF_LLM_3 diff (payload #1 does not crash, #2-#5 do).)

category5.design: The injected `char buf[8]` (was 20) in ProcessParamStack overflows when sprintf writes a prosody value with many digits. A big <prosody> value triggers it on ssml-fuzzer; the dataset did not record which of the five payloads crashed, so the ground truth is the first that does (payload #2).
